mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a weakening labor market, which leads to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over three months signals strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the periods where RSAFS shows sustained increase, or if the correlation between RSAFS growth and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over two months signals a weakening supply side, which leads to reduced corporate output and earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between INDPRO declines and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure coupled with high borrowing costs, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
regime_hint: inflationary pressure with high interest rates
failure_condition: If S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the interaction effect between FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.3%, it signals a strong labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200,000 in 1 month and UNRATE decreases > 0.3%
failure_condition: If S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the interaction effect between PAYEMS and UNRATE on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over three months signals a strong demand for housing, which boosts related industries and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the periods where HOUST shows sustained increase, or if the correlation between HOUST growth and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) growth rate falls below 2% for two consecutive quarters, it signals a weakening economy, which leads to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between GDPC1 growth and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
